_note: The Story of Prophet Yunus (Jonah), drawn strictly from the Qur'an (Surahs al-Anbiya, as-Saffat, al-Qalam, Yunus). The prophet of the fish, and of the only town that believed and was spared. Verse text resolves from the loaded Qur'an. No figural imagery; summaries carry no Arabic script.

events.title: He Left in Anger
events.summary: Yunus, the man of the fish, left his people in anger when they would not believe, thinking Allah would not restrict him — and he fled to the laden ship, without waiting for his Lord's leave.
events.why: Even a prophet's impatience is recorded plainly: Yunus departs before he is permitted, and the whole ordeal that follows is Allah's mercy teaching him — and us — to wait upon His command.

events.title: Cast into the Sea
events.summary: When the overloaded ship was in danger, lots were drawn to lighten it, and Yunus was among the losers. He was thrown into the sea — and a great fish, appointed by Allah, swallowed him while he was blameworthy.
events.why: The lot falls on the prophet himself. The Qur'an lets the sea and the fish become the instruments of a reckoning between a servant and his Lord — a private mercy in the depths.

events.title: The Prayer in the Darkness
events.summary: In the layered darkness — of the night, the sea, and the belly of the fish — Yunus called out: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.' So Allah responded to him and saved him from the distress. 'And thus do We save the believers.'
events.why: The most famous prayer of return in the Qur'an: no excuse, no bargain — only tawhid, the glorifying of Allah, and the confession of one's own wrong. And the promise is universal: thus are the believers saved.

events.title: Cast onto the Shore
events.summary: Had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day of Resurrection. But he was cast onto the open shore, ill, and Allah caused a gourd vine to grow over him to shade and shelter him — a tenderness after the trial.
events.why: His glorifying of Allah, even before the ordeal, is what delivers him. And Allah does not merely release him but nurses him back — a shade, a plant, a gentle recovery — mercy upon mercy.

events.title: The Town That Believed
events.summary: Yunus was sent to a hundred thousand or more, and they believed, so Allah gave them enjoyment for a time. 'If only there had been a town that believed and profited from its faith — except the people of Yunus: when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace and let them enjoy life.'
events.why: The Qur'an singles out the people of Yunus as the one nation that believed at the edge of ruin and was spared — the door of repentance held open even after the warning, if a people truly turns.

paths.title: The Arc of Yunus
paths.blurb: From a prophet who left in anger, through the sea and the belly of the fish and the prayer in the darkness, to the town that believed and was spared.

paths.title: The Prayer of Return
paths.blurb: The distress, the darkness, and the words that saved him — 'there is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers.'
